cards.text: Out in Israel's camp, there's a young man whose mother is an Israelite and whose father is an Egyptian. He goes out among the Israelites, and a fight breaks out between him and an Israelite man. The text never says what the fight was about, and I'm not about to make it up.

cards.question: In the middle of that fight, what does the son of the Israelite woman do?

answers.text: He blasphemes the Name with a curse
He strikes the other man down
He runs away from the camp

cards.text: So they bring him to Moses, Israel's leader. And right here the text stops to name his mother: Shelomith daughter of Dibri.

cards.question: Shelomith daughter of Dibri, the blasphemer's mother, is from which tribe of Israel?

cards.text: Moses has a man in front of him who blasphemed the Name, and nobody rushes this one. I respect that, friend, because I rushed a batch once and pulled out cookies you could SKIP across a lake.

cards.question: While they wait, what do they do with the blasphemer?

answers.text: They send him back to his tent
They hand him over to his family

cards.question: They hold the blasphemer until the will of the ___ is made clear to them.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses. First thing: take the blasphemer outside the camp.

cards.question: Outside the camp, who does the LORD say lays their hands on the blasphemer's head?
And who does the LORD say is to stone the blasphemer?

answers.text: The men of the tribe of Dan

cards.text: But the LORD isn't done. He gives Moses words for all the Israelites, and it starts plain: “If anyone curses his God, he shall bear the consequences of his sin.”

cards.question: The LORD says the law against blaspheming His name covers native Israelites but not foreign residents.

cards.text: Then the law moves from words to actions. If a man takes the life of anyone else, he must surely be put to death.

cards.question: What if someone kills an animal instead of a person? What does the LORD say he must do?

cards.text: Next the LORD covers what happens when someone injures his neighbor. Friend, with a mustache this big, I've bumped into every neighbor I've ever had.

cards.question: Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. What's the idea behind that rule?

answers.text: The penalty is twice the injury
The injured man names the penalty

cards.text: Then the LORD sets the two cases side by side. Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death.

cards.question: To close, the LORD says who gets the same standard of law. Who is it?

answers.text: The foreign resident and the native

cards.question: What reason does the LORD give for one standard of law for everyone?

answers.text: He is the LORD their God
The tribes asked Him for it
Moses could not judge each case

cards.question: Moses speaks to the Israelites, and they take the blasphemer outside the camp and stone him, just as the LORD commanded Moses.

findings.problem: The card calls him a "young man." The text only calls him "the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father" (Lev 24:10) and gives no age. Calling him young adds a detail the text never gives.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answer, "He blasphemes the Name with a curse," uses Bible phrasing ("the Name"). The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ("strikes the other man down," "runs away from the camp"). The right answer stands out as the one that sounds like Scripture.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Verse 16 is the heart of the law the LORD gives: whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must surely be put to death, and the whole assembly must stone him. No card tells this. Card 12 only asks whether the law covers foreign residents. The baker never hears the general law that blasphemy carries the death penalty for everyone, which is the point the passage is making.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action in the verse. Verse 19 is about injuring a neighbor, and the comparison is about bumping into neighbors with his mustache, which is a different action. It also leans on the mustache, which is not meant to be his main source of jokes. And it invents a history of "every neighbor I've ever had," which his backstory doesn't include.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
